blocks.md: This lesson follows **Trajectory Preference Optimization** in *Trajectory Fine-Tuning* (Vol III).

blocks.source: Vol III, Trajectory Fine-Tuning, § Trajectory Preference Optimization
blocks.md: Consider two independently collected continuations of the connection-pool repair that start from identical diagnostic context and both resolve the leak. One continuation runs the entire integration test suite after every minor edit, while the other runs targeted unit tests and executes the full suite only upon completion. Supervised imitation of both trajectories teaches the agent wasteful verification habits alongside disciplined ones; training only on the efficient path discards the signal that the slower trajectory was functionally correct yet needlessly expensive.

questions.q: The section **Trajectory Preference Optimization** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: When several admissible continuations succeed but differ in cost or risk, DPO over selected spans raises the preferred record's reference-relative score against the dispreferred one from an identical context.
Token averaging and example averaging weight trajectories differently, so segmentation and microbatching silently re-weight the corpus unless the normalization rule is fixed.
A corpus with one static tool signature lets the policy memorize argument keys, so augmentation transforms the whole decision context coherently and robustness is measured on held-out schemas.
LoRA cuts trainable parameters but parameter state falls only by the byte ratio of trainable to frozen state, and adapters give modularity, not isolation.
